text:
katie: Heads up — vendor sent a revised commitment term this morning. They introduced a per-pod latency credit but it’s capped and excludes preemptible-to-dedicated conversions. Copying the snippet they sent below.

katie: ```Vendor proposed clause:
If Redwood experiences sustained pod-level p95 request latency > 350ms for more than 10% of the hourly windows, Vendor will issue a service credit equal to 2% of the monthly committed GPU fee for each 24-hour period of breach, capped at 10% monthly. Credits do not apply to capacity impacted by preemptible conversions or customer-initiated region failovers.```

ryan: Hmm that exclusion is rough. Does the clause define what they mean by "preemptible conversions"? can we get a firm definition or a time-window carveout?

katie: They used the vendor term; I asked for clarification — they mean any migration from preemptible/spot instances to reserved due to reclaim, but they didn't commit to a quantitative threshold.

soumya: Also, our March invoice shows a ~7% higher usage in us-west2 than expected during the reclaim event on 2025-12-03. I flagged a potential metering mismatch — could be double-billed vGPU attach/detach churn. @billing-bot can you pull the attach/detach counts for that day?

billing-bot: ```query: GET /billing/usage?start=2025-12-03T00:00:00Z&end=2025-12-04T00:00:00Z&resource=gpu
result: total_gpu_hours=13420, attach_ops=3821, detach_ops=3779, reconciled_charges=@storage_layer: 0.02% discrepancy flagged```

jen: That many attach/detach ops could definitely push us into extra metering buckets if the vendor meters by attach rather than sustained allocation. We should ask vendor for metering granularity and whether they support amortized billing for short-lived reattachments.

andre: Negotiation idea: ask for two parallel remedies — (1) a hard monthly credit floor (e.g., min 5% if we hit any provider-level availability hit affecting >X% capacity) and (2) an invoice reconciliation clause for metering anomalies with 30-day dispute window. That protects both SLO and billing drift.

vendor_rep: Appreciate the feedback. We can do a limited concession: increase the credit cap to 12% monthly for provider-side infrastructure outages, and add a reconciliation process for metering disputes, but we need to exclude customer misconfigurations and rapid reattach churn under 5 minutes.

ryan: The 5-minute exclusion is concerning — our autoscaler sometimes reattaches to recover shards in ~2–3 minutes. That would exclude a lot. Can we instead define exclusion as reattachments that exceed X ops/min sustained for 15 minutes?

vendor_rep: I can take that back. Proposed compromise: exclude reattachments with back-to-back ops > 300 per 5 minutes at the account level. Otherwise they qualify.

katie: Action items: (1) @vendor_rep, please send formal redline with the 12% cap and the reconciliation clause language; (2) @billing-bot, export the attach/detach histogram for December and Jan at 1-min granularity so we can show typical autoscaler behavior; (3) @jen + @andre, draft fallback language for hard floor credit (5%) we can push if vendor stalls.

soumya: I'll also pull pod-level p95 latency aggregates for the same outage window so we can map latency breaches to reattach storms.

vendor_rep: Will do a redline by EOD PDT. I can also propose a short pilot: reserve a small regional pool with strict SLA for 3 months so you can validate metering behavior before committing to full EDP.

katie: Pilot sounds good. Let's prioritize the reconciliation clause — if we get that, I'm more comfortable with the rest. :+1:

ryan: Thanks — I'll compile our counter language and drop it here by 11:30 PT.

andre: If vendor pushes back on the floor credit, escalate to sales/legal. We need commercial leverage.

katie: Agreed. I'll loop in sales after vendor redline. Thanks everyone.
